001_N: ["Day thirty. The sun is right there. You can see it through the window, rippling, about sixty feet above your head.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
002_N: ["You could swim up in under a minute. And if you did, it could kill you.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
003_N: ["So what if you lived underwater for thirty days?",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
004_N: ["Not in a submarine. In a real underwater home, the kind people actually live in.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
005_N: ["It's called Aquarius. It sits on the sea floor off the Florida Keys, several miles from shore, and it's roughly the size of a school bus.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
006_N: ["Day one. You and your crew dive down with your bags, swim under the habitat, and climb up a ladder... into the living room.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
007_N: ["Because your front door is a hole in the floor. Right below it is the open ocean.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
008_N: ["So why doesn't the water rush in? Because the air in here is squeezed to the same pressure as the sea outside. About two and a half times what you breathe on land.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
009_N: ["The water pushes up. The air pushes back. It's a tie, and the sea just... stays out.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
010_N: ["Everything you breathe comes down a long hose from a big buoy floating on the surface. The same buoy sends you electricity and a phone line, and someone on shore watches over you around the clock.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
011_N: ["Your ears pop. The air feels thick and damp. And something is already happening inside your body that you can't feel at all.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
012_N: ["Every breath here carries extra nitrogen, the same gas that makes up most of normal air. Under this pressure, it slowly soaks into your blood, your muscles, your fat.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
013_N: ["Think of a bottle of soda. The gas is pressed into the liquid, so you don't see any bubbles. Until you open the cap.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
014_N: ["Your body is now that bottle. If you shot up to the surface, the nitrogen would come out as bubbles, in your joints, in your blood, even in your spinal cord.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
015_N: ["Doctors call it decompression sickness. Divers call it the bends, because people used to bend over from the pain.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
016_N: ["In the eighteen seventies, the men who dug the foundations of the Brooklyn Bridge worked in pressurized chambers under the river.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
017_N: ["When they came up too fast, some collapsed. Several died.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
018_N: ["Even the chief engineer, Washington Roebling, was left partly paralyzed. He watched the rest of the bridge go up through a telescope, while his wife Emily carried his orders to the site.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
019_N: ["The fix came from a Scottish scientist, John Scott Haldane, in the early nineteen hundreds. He tested it on goats.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
020_N: ["He put them under pressure, then brought them back up in slow, careful stages, with stops along the way. The goats that came up slowly were fine.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
021_N: ["Those stops are still the basic idea behind every dive table today. You can thank a goat.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
022_N: ["So here's the deal you made. After about a day down here, your body is full. Saturated. It can't hold any more nitrogen at this depth.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
023_N: ["And that's actually good news. It means the way back up takes the same time whether you stay one day or a month. About seventeen hours.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
024_N: ["Seventeen hours, in a sealed room, before you're allowed to see the sky. Remember that number.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
025_N: ["Day three. You start to notice what home really means down here.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
026_N: ["Bunks stacked like shelves. A tiny table. A microwave and a hot water tap. That's the whole kitchen.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
027_N: ["Dinner is mostly freeze-dried food from a bag. And it tastes like... nothing.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
028_N: ["Aquanauts say the pressure dulls their sense of taste, so they pour hot sauce on almost everything. Nobody has properly tested why. But ask anyone who's lived down here, and they'll ask you to pass the bottle.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
029_N: ["Then there's the damp. The air is always wet. Towels never really dry.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
030_N: ["Ear and skin infections are a real risk down here. Aquanauts even have a name for it: the creeping crud.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
031_N: ["You start cleaning your ears like it's your job. Because down here, it kind of is.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
032_N: ["Day seven. And now the strangest part: you're not stuck inside at all.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
033_N: ["Since your body is already saturated, you can drop through the front door and work outside for hours every day, without the time limits normal divers have.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
034_N: ["A normal diver at this depth gets about an hour before they have to head up. You get the whole afternoon.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
035_N: ["You count fish, measure coral, and swim back home for lunch. Your commute is ten seconds and one ladder.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
036_N: ["And Aquarius is the only undersea research lab of its kind still working anywhere in the world. Scientists come here to study the coral reef from the inside, day and night.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
037_N: ["And the sea is loud. All around you there's a constant crackling, like bacon frying in a pan.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
038_N: ["It's snapping shrimp. Thousands of them, slamming their claws shut so fast they make tiny exploding bubbles.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
039_N: ["After a few hours out there, you're cold to the bone, even in warm Florida water. Water pulls heat out of your body much faster than air does.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
040_N: ["It's so much like space that NASA sends its astronauts here to train. They practice spacewalks on the sea floor, sealed off from the world, just like you.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
041_N: ["Day ten. You wake up and have no idea what time it is.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
042_N: ["Your body keeps time with sunlight. Bright light in the morning tells your brain to wake up. Darkness tells it to sleep.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
043_N: ["Down here, the light through the window is a dim blue twilight, and inside it's lamps, all the time. Without bright sunlight, your inner clock can drift. You yawn at noon and stare at the ceiling at three in the morning.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
044_N: ["And there's another thing the sun does for you. When it hits your skin, your body makes vitamin D, which you need for strong bones and a healthy immune system.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
045_N: ["No sun, no vitamin D. When Fabien Cousteau, the grandson of the famous explorer Jacques Cousteau, lived in Aquarius for thirty-one days, he came out pale, with his vitamin D down.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
046_N: ["Your crewmates start to look like they've been living in a basement. Because, technically, they have.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
047_N: ["Day twelve. A handful of people, one school bus, and no door you can open.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
048_N: ["Little things start to feel big. The way someone chews. The way someone hums. Crews who live in tight spaces, from submarines to space stations, learn the same rules: talk early, stay kind, and take turns at the window.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
050_N: ["It's the surface crew. There's a call for you from home. Someone you love is in the hospital.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
051_N: ["On land, you'd grab your keys and go. Down here, the fastest way out is still seventeen hours in a sealed room.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
052_N: ["So you have a choice. Quit the mission, and spend those hours staring at a wall, unable to call, unable to help. Or stay, finish the work, and hope.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
053_N: ["This is the real price of living underwater. Not the food, not the damp. It's that the world goes on without you, and you can't just leave.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
054_N: ["You decide to stay. The news, a few hours later, is good. But you won't forget the feeling of being sixty feet away from everything.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
055_N: ["And you're not the first to feel it.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
056_N: ["In nineteen sixty-three, Jacques Cousteau's team built a starfish-shaped house on the floor of the Red Sea, and lived in it for a month. His film about it, World Without Sun, won an Oscar.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
057_N: ["In nineteen sixty-five, the U.S. Navy sank a lab called SEALAB Two, more than two hundred feet down off California.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
058_N: ["So deep that the crew breathed a mix with helium in it. Which made every one of them sound like a cartoon duck.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
059_N: ["Astronaut Scott Carpenter stayed down for thirty days. A trained dolphin named Tuffy carried tools and mail to the crew. And when the President called to congratulate him, he had trouble understanding a word Carpenter said.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
060_N: ["Why the duck voice? Sound travels much faster through helium than through normal air, and that pushes every voice way up.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
061_N: ["Today, divers still live this way for work. Commercial saturation divers fix pipelines and oil platforms hundreds of feet down. They spend weeks in pressurized chambers on ships, and coming back to normal pressure can take days.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
062_N: ["Day twenty-five. Something unexpected happens. You stop counting the days.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
063_N: ["The tiny house feels normal. The fish outside the window have names. The crew are your family now.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
064_N: ["And the idea of going up starts to feel... strange.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
065_N: ["Fabien Cousteau said exactly this after his thirty-one days. He felt like he could stay down another month, and coming up, he was almost panicking.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
066_N: ["And his crew didn't just survive. They brought back enough data for at least ten scientific studies about the reef outside their window.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
067_N: ["Day twenty-nine. Decompression day. The hatch is sealed, and the pressure inside is lowered, very, very slowly.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
068_N: ["Hour by hour, the nitrogen leaves your body the gentle way, through your lungs, one breath at a time.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
069_N: ["You play cards. You sleep. You stare at the wall. Seventeen hours.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
070_N: ["Day thirty. You swim up through the blue, and break the surface.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
071_N: ["The sunlight is almost painful. The air smells like salt and boat fuel, and it's the best thing you've ever smelled.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
072_N: ["Your body made it. A little pale, a little low on vitamin D, with very clean ears. But fine.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
073_N: ["Back on land, doctors check you over. Blood tests, skin, ears, lungs. Then they hand you the best prescription you've ever gotten: go stand in the sun.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
074_N: ["And a month is not even close to the record. In twenty twenty-three, Joseph Dituri lived a hundred days in a small underwater lodge in Key Largo.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
075_N: ["He wanted to find out whether living under extra pressure might actually be good for the human body. Scientists are still studying the results.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
076_N: ["Then in January twenty twenty-five, a German engineer, Rüdiger Koch, spent a hundred and twenty days in a capsule off the coast of Panama.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
077_N: ["So, could you live underwater for thirty days? Your body, yes. It's tougher than it looks.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
078_N: ["The hard part is everything else. The damp, the dark, and knowing that the way home takes seventeen hours.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
079_N: ["Would you go? Tell me in the comments. And subscribe, so you don't miss the next one.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89","speed":0.9}]
